title: Dark chocolate chilli bark
subtitle: dark chocolate with dried chilli and sea salt
excerpt: Dark chocolate chilli bark is a thin, snappable slab of melted dark chocolate flavoured with dried chilli flakes and finished with sea salt flakes. It takes 10 minutes to make, sets in the fridge in an hour, and breaks into irregular shards for serving. The chilli heat is subtle, it arrives a few seconds after the chocolate flavour, warming rather than burning.
sourceNotes: Chocolate bark, thin, free-form slabs of melted chocolate with toppings, became a mainstream home confectionery project in the early 2000s, popularised by food bloggers and gift-food culture. The pairing of dark chocolate with chilli has pre-Columbian origins in Mesoamerica, where cacao was consumed as a bitter, spiced drink long before European sugar-sweetened versions existed. The bark form is modern; the flavour combination is ancient. Dried chilli and sea salt as a chocolate coating appeared widely in artisan chocolate from the 2000s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 weeks ahead. Store away from strong-smelling foods.

content.text: Dark chocolate chilli bark is a thin snappable slab of melted chocolate with a slow-burn heat from dried chilli and a clean mineral finish from sea salt. It is one of the simplest confectionery projects there is: melt, pour, scatter, set. The critical point is not to overheat the chocolate or add chilli before the chocolate is off the heat, both kill the flavour.

Put the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, making sure the base of the bowl does not touch the water. Stir gently until melted and smooth. Do not let the chocolate get above 50°C or it will seize and become grainy. Remove the bowl from the heat as soon as the last piece has melted.

Line a large baking tray with parchment paper. Pour the melted chocolate onto the tray and spread it out to a thin, even layer, about 3 to 4 mm thick. Scatter the chilli flakes and sea salt flakes over the surface. Tilt the tray slightly to spread any pooled chocolate, then lay it flat.

Refrigerate for 1 hour until completely set and firm. Lift the parchment onto a board and break the bark into irregular shards by pressing down along natural fault lines. Avoid cutting with a knife as the chocolate tends to shatter unpredictably. Store in an airtight container in a cool place, not in the fridge, as condensation causes bloom.
